title: Privacy: an erase that neither the cloud nor the device copy took was kept only in memory, and a reload brought the record back
evidence: packages/health-core/src/record-session-erase.ts eraseSession: when the cloud definitely refused the write and the failure mirror did not land (cloud tier; save-state writtenNowhere), the session puts back its pre-erase copy, clearedFor and saveWarning, and answers { success: false } with no reason. A definite refusal is one named predicate, packages/health-core/src/write-refusal.ts isDefiniteRefusal (owner ruling A): a ConflictError (never a LostUpdateError), a full store, WritesStoppedError, or HTTP 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 412, 413 or 422, each reasoned per provider beside the table. Everything else may have landed: SyncManager marks it (uncertainWrite) and keeps its words; Google Drive's adapter marks every failure after it sent the upload. A pass that started before the erase's swap never carries its landed mark into the erase (N1). Before, the failed mirror write was swallowed (record-session.ts persist catch) while the page showed the erased record (web: own-end with 'Cloud sync failed - your latest changes are still on this device'; iPhone: EraseText.notSent 'Your record is erased on this iPhone'). The pending marker stays set: it lifts only the pre-erase copy into a pre-erase cloud. Steps before the write are not undone: chat tombstones and, on the web, the reminders teardown (S59). NOT fixed, stated: when the cloud did not answer (or answered 408, 429 or 5xx) AND the device copy could not be written, behaviour stays as today: the erased copy is held in memory and retried, the words still say it is erased here (S58's gap), and a reload or relaunch before a retry lands brings the record back. A second try of the device write in that case was not added (record-session.ts sits at the file cap); it is left for S54. Other residuals: Google Drive's last version check runs inside the step its adapter marks uncertain, so a 4xx on that check, before any upload, also keeps the erased copy in memory, as today (drive-rest.ts driveUpdateIfVersion; drive-rest.ts is over the file cap, so not split here); a remote change folded in by a pass that landed during the erase is dropped from memory by the put-back and comes back at the next read (the cloud's copy wins the merge); the web device tier has the same shape (a guest erase whose localStorage write fails says SAVE_FAILED and shows the erased copy until a reload) and is not changed here. Checks: packages/health-core/src/record-session.erase-mirror.test.ts (the refusal table, N1, the put-back, the landed and unanswered cases), widget-src/src/storage/roadmap-store-erase-mirror.test.ts, ios/engine/cloud.test.ts. US-11 AC3b, AC7; US-16 AC2a
